rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 18, BOOK VII, CHAPTER 3 OF THE ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to provide that a license should not expire, given that the licensee has made timely and sufficient application for its renewal until finally determined by the relevant department, agency or branch of government.
Aims to amend the provision for non-expiration to also include franchises and specifically provides that inaction on a pending application must not be considered denial of the application.
Intends to encourage concerned agencies or branches of government to act on applications for renewal of franchises and licenses promptly and resolutely.

rows.title_full:
AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE RIGHT OF THE PEOPLE TO FREE EXPRESSION, TO
PEACEABLY ASSEMBLE, AND TO PETITION THE GOVERNMENT FOR
REDRESS OF GRIEVANCES, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE BATAS
PAMBANSA BLG. 880 OR THE “PUBLIC ASSEMBLY ACT OF 1985”
rows.title_short: New Public Assembly Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to ensure the free exercise of the fundamental rights of the people without unnecessary and unreasonable impediments.

Mandates any person or group who intends to organize and hold a public assembly in a public place which includes any highway, boulevard, avenue, road, street, bridge or other thoroughfare, park, plaza, square, or any open space where people are allowed access to serve a notice to the city or municipal mayor who has jurisdiction over the place where the assembly is to be held except freedom park duly established by law or ordinance, private property with the consent of the owner of the person entitled to its legal possession, or in the campus of a government-owned and operated educational institution, subject to its rules and regulations.

Provides the responsibilities of leader and organizers of a public assembly; guidelines and rules of conduct, prohibited acts and penalties, among others.
rows.status: Pending With Rules (Included in OB on 2020-11-16)

rows.title_full:
AN ACT CREATING A SYSTEM OF PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN LOCAL
GOVERNMENTS AND CIVIL SOCIETY ORGANIZATIONS THROUGH THE
ESTABLISHMENT OF A PEOPLE'S COUNCIL IN EVERY LOCAL
GOVERNMENT UNIT, PRESCRIBING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS AND
PROVIDING FOR ITS PARTICIPATION IN THE LOCAL SANGGUNIAN AND
LOCAL BOARDS, COUNCILS, COMMITTEES, TASK FORCES OR SIMILAR
WORK GROUPS
rows.title_short: People Empowerment Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to ensure participation of citizens in all avenues of local governance by creating a mechanism where citizens´ views and opinions may be heard and considered.

Allow Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) to be duly recognized and allowed to participate in local governance provided they have actively operated for at least one (1) year in the city or municipality where majority of its members reside, and must apply for accreditation with the local sanggunian.

Defines the functions of the Committee for the Accreditation of CSOs; Enumerates the rights and privileges of the accredited CSOs; Creates the People´s Councils which shall determine its own organizational structure and internal rules, among others.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2021-01-18, transmitted to the Senate on 2021-01-19 and received by the Senate on 2021-01-19

rows.author: I034
rows.title_full:
AN ACT

PROVIDING FOR PROTECTION OF THE REMITTANCES OF

OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS
rows.title_short: Overseas Filipino Workers ( O F Ws ) Remittance Protection Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to 1.) provide for a mandatory discount of 50% of the remittance fees imposed by bank and non-bank financial intermediaries; 2.)  provide for tax incentives to intermediaries which shall provide for such discounts; 3.) prohibit intermediaries from raising their current remittances fees without prior consultation with the Department of Finance (DOF), Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), and the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA).

Mandates government agencies to provide financial education programs to OFWs and their families.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2020-12-15, transmitted to the Senate on 2020-12-16 and received by the Senate on 2020-12-16

rows.author: I105
rows.title_full:
AN ACT REDUCING WASTAGE BY DONATING AND
RECYCLING EXCESS EDIBLE FOOD
rows.title_short: Food Surplus Reduction Act
rows.abstract:
Aims to attain food security, end hunger, and promote the efficient use of the country´s food resources through food redistribution and recycling.

Mandates the different government departments, agencies and LGUs headed by the National Nutrition Council (NNC)  to undertake a National Zero-Food Waste Campaign to raise awareness on the impact of a food surplus and strategies to decrease wasted food starting at the household level and promote the food surplus reduction hierarchy and recommend means of reducing individual food waste.

Provides steps to be followed in the distribution of edible food surplus; procedure on food-related business surplus reduction strategy; guidelines and standards on National Food Surplus Scheme; enumerates the responsibility of LGUs in Waste Reduction Strategy; imposes penalties for selling food donations and causing edible food surplus to be unfit for human consumption, among others.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2020-12-14, transmitted to the Senate on 2020-12-15 and received by the Senate on 2020-12-15
